name: N-body galaxy
doc: A few thousand softened, mutually gravitating stars (direct all-pairs sum on the GPU, tiled through workgroup memory) orbiting a central mass in a disk, seen from a slowly orbiting, tilted camera and drawn as additive glowing points with a core glow. Bass makes the central mass heavier, so the disk is pulled in and spins up; each onset kicks the velocities with a two-armed radial shove that differential rotation winds into spiral arms. Birth radius and speed pick the palette colour.

palette.doc: stop 0 is the backdrop; the inner disk takes the top stops, the outskirts the low ones

count.doc: number of stars (rounded to 256); the cost grows with its square

core.doc: central mass, in units of the disk's mass

pull.doc: how much the bass adds to the central mass (fraction)

kick.doc: onset velocity kick, as a fraction of the orbital speed (0 = off)

cool.doc: relaxation toward circular orbits per second: keeps a readable disk

dust.doc: every 7th star is a big dim dust puff (0 = off)

tilt.doc: camera elevation above the disk plane, radians
